17: How much time and how many people will you need from our side?
18: The CEO or a member of the leadership team is needed at kick-off, during prioritisation and for key decisions. 19: Is this consulting, implementation, or a temporary stand-in for an internal Head of AI?
20: All three — in that order. The sprint is implementation with a mandate; the retainer is a fractional Head of AI. And when the AI agenda grows into a full-time role, I will help you find an internal Head of AI, onboard them and hand over a working system — the register, the rules, the agents and the metrics. I do not finish by leaving; I finish by handing over.
21: How do you handle data security and accountability for AI workers?
22: I build vendor-neutral: frontier models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) are chosen by the task, not by partnership. Company data stays in your systems — agents access it through APIs with controlled permissions, and nothing spills into anyone else's training data. Every agent has a defined point where a human decides, and an owner who is accountable for the output. Every deployment has an internal owner, defined permissions, auditable operation and human approval rules. We use least privilege, minimisation of the data passed on, controlled fallbacks and the ability to roll an action back. No system goes into production if it is not clear who is accountable for its decisions and outputs.
23: What are the payment terms and what is not included in the price?
24: The 90-day mandate costs CZK 750,000 excl. VAT and is invoiced in three monthly payments of CZK 250,000 excl. VAT, each before the corresponding 30-day phase begins. For the first payment you receive a complete decision pack — a map of AI activities, priorities with an estimated impact in CZK, and a recommendation to continue or to stop. External licences, cloud and third-party services are not included unless stated otherwise. The client approves each such cost in advance and pays the supplier directly. I accept no commissions for recommending technology. The fractional retainer is invoiced monthly in advance.
25: We have never had a Head of AI. Why do we need one right now?
26: Perhaps you don't yet. This role starts to make sense the moment AI affects revenue, costs, company data, customers or how employees make decisions. Without a clear owner the AI agenda does not stop — its direction is effectively set by employees, IT and suppliers according to their own priorities. The job of a Head of AI is not to add another layer of management, but to unify accountability, stop weak experiments and concentrate investment where it has measurable impact. If AI is still only a side experiment, you do not need this role yet.

318: Will you help us with the EU AI Act?
319: Yes, to the extent that genuinely applies to you — and without scaremongering.
320: Most companies are not providers of a high-risk AI system. What most often applies to you is Article 4 and, depending on how you deploy AI, also Article 50.
321: Article 4 (AI literacy) has applied since 2 February 2025. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — the Digital Omnibus on AI, which entered into force on 27 July 2026 — changed its wording: you do not have to guarantee a specific level of literacy for every individual, but you must still take appropriate measures to support its development. It is an obligation of effort, not of guaranteed result.
322: The transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, depending on the company's role and how AI is used. For providers of systems generating synthetic content that were on the market before that date, a transitional period until 2 December 2026 applies to Article 50(2).
323: The main obligations for high-risk systems apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and from 2 August 2028 (Annex I).
324: I set up governance at your company primarily for the sake of control over data and accountability. Regulatory compliance is a consequence, not the main reason. I am not a lawyer, and the final legal assessment belongs to your legal counsel — I supply the groundwork, not a legal opinion.
